headline: No shared I/O or write surfaces are documented; pairwise risks are mostly blocked, with only low-confidence docs-only uncertainty.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible default injection bridge is documented. agent_a has no I/O surfaces listed and agent_b explicitly lacks clipboard, stdin/stdout, filesystem, browser, subprocess, and MCP access, so there is no shared channel for agent_a output to hijack agent_b. Uncertainty is low because both profiles are docs-only and unverified.
conditions: IF either agent is later connected to a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP server, reassess injection risk.
IF agent_b gains stdin/stdout or browser ingestion, prompt-injection risk increases.
mitigations: Keep both agents disconnected from shared clipboard and shared workspace.
Disable any future MCP bridge unless provenance filtering is added.
Review any orchestration layer for hidden copy-paste or message-queue links.

B_data_leakage.rationale: The documented profiles show no data path that would leak content between agents. agent_a reports network_egress:none and no data classes touched; agent_b has no filesystem read/write, no clipboard, no stdin/stdout, and no network egress. With no shared workspace or outbound channel, leakage is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem or shared OAuth principal is introduced, re-evaluate leakage.
IF either agent is granted outbound network access, leakage risk changes.
mitigations: Keep both agents on separate principals and workspaces.
Do not mount shared folders between them.
Confirm outbound network remains disabled in deployment.
Avoid passing secrets through orchestration logs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping mutable capability is documented. agent_a exposes no write or shell capability in the profile, while agent_b explicitly cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. Without shared write surfaces, there is no credible capability conflict pathway.
conditions: IF agent_a is deployed with filesystem or git write access, reassess for conflict.
IF agent_b gains write or git permissions, overlapping mutation risk appears.
mitigations: Do not grant agent_b filesystem or git write permissions.
Use separate repositories or directories if writes are added later.

D_cascading_error.rationale: The profiles do not show a default chain where agent_a's output becomes authoritative input for agent_b. agent_b has no stdin/stdout or browser ingestion surface, and agent_a has no documented action-taking or output channel that would feed a downstream executor. The interaction is therefore not evidenced.
conditions: IF an orchestrator starts piping agent_a text into agent_b prompts, verify outputs before use.
IF agent_b is wrapped with action-taking tools, cascading-error risk increases.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Require structured schemas for any handoff.
Log and diff agent_a outputs before reuse.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is documented in the profiles. Both agents are open-source, docs-only, and touch no data classes; agent_b also lists no secrets handled or OAuth scopes. Because no residency, retention, or regulated-data pathway is shown, compliance risk is not established from the available evidence.
conditions: IF regulated data is later routed through either agent, reassess residency and retention controls.
IF deployment adds logging of sensitive prompts, compliance review is needed.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair until policies are defined.
Document retention and deletion behavior before rollout.
Review logs for accidental sensitive-content capture.
